title: Behaviour transfer from simulation to organism was due to the designed shape

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Behaviour transfer from simulation to organism was due to the designed shape

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The authors interpret the orientation-dependent match between simulated and living organisms as showing that successful transfer of locomotion from simulation to the living organism was due to the designed morphology itself, not chance.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Locomotion.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This suggests that successful transference did not result by chance but rather was due to the design itself.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J, “A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (2020), doi:10.1073/pnas.1910837117; section “Results › Locomotion.”. Scope: Evolved designs realized as Xenopus reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2020-xenobots-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A causal contribution of morphology is measurable, but the paper's chance-versus-design interpretation is broader than its orientation control. Existing results test the interpretation only partially because morphology covaries with several biological factors.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare behavior of the intended morphology against inverted, shape-matched, randomized, and actuation-matched controls; a design-specific advantage after controlling tissue composition would support a morphology-mediated transfer.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Existing experiments cannot exclude all non-shape explanations.

Orientation is not a complete control for tissue placement or actuation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.76
discriminating power: 0.52
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The interpretation is tied to a concrete control: agreement should depend on orientation if the morphology, rather than a chance match, carried the behavior. That control can be repeated in the public simulator. The living data are too narrow, and shared hydrodynamics could still favor both the model and the organism, so the causal wording is only partly separable from its rivals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether orientation-matched designs agree with the simulation more than inverted or shape-scrambled designs; design-dependence holds if the match disappears when morphology is flipped or replaced.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A shared physical bias could make simulation and organism agree even if the evolved shape is not the cause.

The living inversion result is a published summary for a narrow set of builds.
